_: Routes that change state with no role check, on purpose. Read by scripts/role-check-sweep.mjs.
Each entry names one route exactly and says why no role applies. An entry that matches
nothing any more fails the check: drop it in the same change that removed the route.
Routes without member authentication are never findings, so they need no entry here:
- /api/v1/internal/*: behind the internal secret (plugins/internal-auth.ts), called by our
own workers and engine, never by a member;
- incoming webhooks (ESPs, payment, integrations): authenticated by the sender's signature
or secret, not by a member session.
Customer webhook *configuration* (POST /api/v1/webhooks and friends) is a member action and
is in the baseline, not here.

exemptions.why: Enrols the caller's own second factor. Every member manages their own login, whatever their role.
Confirms the caller's own second factor.
Removes the caller's own second factor; keyed by the user, not by the organisation.
Re-sends the caller's own email verification.
Issues a session for another organisation the caller is a member of; the role in it comes from that membership (services/auth/cross-account.ts), not from the current one.
The invited person accepts their own invitation; the token is the credential, and the role is the one the invitation carries.
Event ingest from the customer's website (web-sdk), with a publishable key. A publishable key never satisfies a role, so a role check would shut the website out.
Storefront checkout ingest (publishable key); rate-limited per verified key and address.
Serves an on-site call to action to a website visitor (publishable key).
Records a visitor's click on an on-site call to action (publishable key).
Records a visitor dismissing an on-site call to action (publishable key).
Registers a visitor's browser for web push (publishable key).
Unregisters a visitor's browser from web push (publishable key).
A shopper subscribes to a back-in-stock alert on the customer's store (publishable key).
A shopper subscribes to a price-drop alert on the customer's store (publishable key).
Records a newsletter referral conversion from the customer's website (publishable key, scoped to the key's organisation since Z130; before that it had no authentication at all).
